articles.title: Introducing Director 2
articles.summary: This article introduces Radhika Gupta, the new "Director 2," who shares her lifelong passion for astronomy, cultivated through her background in physics and mathematics and a career in software engineering. She expresses her dedication to further exploring the universe with rigor and enthusiasm. The piece appears in the SJAA Ephemeris for March 2024.

articles.title: Introducing Astronomy 101 and Library Program Leaders
articles.summary: This article introduces Carl-Erik Svensson as the new Astro 101 Program Leader for SJAA, detailing his extensive amateur astronomy background including astrophotography, public outreach, and future observatory plans. It also presents David Kershaw as the new Librarian, highlighting his physics education, diverse engineering career, and prior library experience. Both individuals are new volunteer leaders within the organization.

articles.title: Observation Report Total Solar Eclipse
articles.summary: Joseph Fragola and his wife traveled 1,749 miles to Copperas Cove, Texas, to observe the total solar eclipse. Despite initial poor weather forecasts and cloudy conditions on eclipse day, breaks in the clouds allowed them to view totality, although the corona was somewhat muted. They continued to watch the partial phases and captured images using a Seestar S50.

articles.title: Marianne's Meanderings
articles.summary: The author recounts her successful 2024 total solar eclipse observation trip to China Spring, Texas, with family, motivated by a 2017 experience. Despite initial cloud anxiety, the group enjoyed clear views of totality, witnessing phenomena like Bailey's Beads and prominences through various filtered equipment. The experience fostered wonder, especially among the children, and concluded with a 'Planet Walk' activity.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article presents a gallery of astrophotography images contributed by members of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association). Each entry details a deep-sky object captured, such as galaxies and nebulae, along with comprehensive technical specifications including the imaging equipment (telescope, camera, mount), software used for processing, capture dates, and observation locations primarily in California. The gallery serves as a showcase of member talent and their astrophotography setups.

articles.title: Solar Eclipse Trip
articles.summary: The author embarked on a 1,700-mile trip to Killeen, Texas, and later relocated to Grannis, Arkansas, to observe a solar eclipse. Despite initial poor weather forecasts and thick clouds on the day, a last-minute decision to move south led them to a patch of clear sky, allowing them to witness and photograph the total eclipse. They captured memorable photos even with a simplified setup, including views of the corona and prominences, and also used an H-alpha telescope upon returning to the campsite.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: This article from the SJAA Board of Directors announces the re-election of the President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with the Vice President position remaining open. It details new appointments for Librarian and Astronomy 101 leader, along with several vacant volunteer positions, including Ephemeris Editors and Mendoza Ranch program leaders. Excerpts from recent board meetings highlight discussions on planning a swap meet, approving funds for solar equipment and a filter repair, and addressing resignations.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers a diverse range of programs and resources designed for its members and the broader community. These include a library, free telescope repair sessions, regular solar observing events, and introductory programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky. Additionally, SJAA provides an equipment loaner program, hosts an Astro Imaging Special Interest Group and workshops, and conducts school star parties, with many offerings exclusive to members to support astronomy enthusiasts.
